thermify

Efficient, reproducible and spatially explicit agroclimatic thermal indices in R.

thermify computes heat and chill accumulation indices from daily or hourly temperatures, and from monthly climatologies such as WorldClim after a mean-preserving temporal densification.

Family Methods
Growing degree-days average, single sine, single triangle, double sine, double triangle; horizontal, vertical and intermediate upper cutoffs; degree-hours
Chilling hours analytical sine and triangle estimates from daily extremes; counts on hourly data
Chill units Utah model (Richardson et al. 1974)
Chill portions Dynamic model (Fishman et al. 1987; Erez et al. 1990), resumable across blocks
Temporal reconstruction monthly to daily (pchip_mp, natively or via tempify); daily to hourly (sine or Linvill)
Spatial block-wise processing of terra::SpatRaster stacks, GeoTIFF and NetCDF output

[!IMPORTANT] Monthly climate normals are not daily or hourly observations. Indices reconstructed from monthly climatologies are model-based estimates and must be validated against observations before decision-critical use.

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("djwillichile/thermify@v0.1.0")   # release
remotes::install_github("djwillichile/thermify")          # development

terra is needed for raster workflows. The optional tempify backend needs Python and reticulate; without it thermify uses an equivalent native R engine.

Quick start 

library(thermify)

tmin <- c(4, 8, 12, 15)
tmax <- c(16, 22, 28, 34)

# Growing degree-days (degC day)
degree_days(tmin, tmax, method = "single_sine", base = 10)
degree_days(tmin, tmax, method = "single_sine", base = 10, upper = 30,
            cutoff = "vertical")

# Chilling hours estimated from daily extremes (h)
chill_hours(c(-2, 4), c(10, 12), method = "sine")

# Hourly series (observed or reconstructed)
hourly <- hourly_temperatures(rep(3, 30), rep(13, 30), latitude = -35.97,
                              doy = 152:181)
chill_units(hourly, method = "utah", output = "total")
chill_portions(hourly, method = "dynamic", output = "total")

From monthly climatology to seasonal indices for one location:

tmin <- c(11.4, 11.1, 9.2, 6.8, 5.3, 3.9, 3.1, 3.6, 4.6, 6.3, 8.4, 10.3)
tmax <- c(29.6, 29.2, 26.5, 21.9, 17.2, 13.9, 13.6, 15.3, 17.9, 21.2,
          24.9, 28.2)
res <- thermify(tmin, tmax, input = "monthly", latitude = -35.97,
                temporal = "auto", interpolation = "pchip_mp",
                indices = c("gdd", "ch", "cu", "cp"))
res$summary

WorldClim 2.1 at 30 arc-seconds can be read for a region only, transferring just the bytes of that window (optionally masked by a polygon):

win  <- study_window(lon = -72.3225, lat = -35.9671, size_km = 20)
tmin <- worldclim_region("tmin", win, path = "data")
tmax <- worldclim_region("tmax", win, path = "data")

When does a crop reach its degree-day requirement, or a cultivar its chill requirement?

# station: data frame with daily date, tmin, tmax from 1 Sep to 30 Apr
gdd <- degree_days(station$tmin, station$tmax, method = "single_sine",
                   base = 10)
threshold_date(gdd, station$date, threshold = 500)

For rasters, thermify_rast() applies the same workflow block by block to 12-layer SpatRaster stacks and writes one file per index, reporting progress (blocks done, elapsed time and estimated time remaining).

Verification

  • Unit tests cover every method against closed forms, numerical integration, an independent transcription of the Dynamic model equations, block equivalence and raster geometry.

  • inst/verification/verify_references.R cross-checks thermify against chillR (Dynamic, Utah, chilling hours, day length, Linvill hours) and degday (UC IPM degree-day formulas). Current differences are below 1e-12, except for one documented convention in the pre-dawn Linvill curve (night = "chillr" reproduces chillR exactly).

  • The native pchip_mp engine reproduces tempify to within 1e-13 degC.

  • About 400 expectations in unit, acceptance (one per user story), integration and error-path tests, with 94 % line coverage; see docs/TESTING.md.

Computational verification is not empirical validation; see vignette("validation") for the station-based protocol.

Case study

examples/cauquenes computes all indices for a 20 x 20 km window around Cauquenes (Maule, Chile) from WorldClim 2.1.
